record.paper_title: Eight Open Problems in Distributed Computing
record.context_brief: Local algorithms on unit disk graphs
record.original_question: For geometric graph models motivated by wireless sensor networks, especially unit disk graphs where geometry constrains node placement and wireless links, what is the local complexity of typical coordination tasks such as computing a dominating set under k-local communication?

evidence.quote: So far, very little is known about local algorithms for geometric graphs.
To give a specific example, even for a simple model known as unit disk graph, the local complexity of typical coordination tasks (e.g., computing a dominating set) is an open problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A unit disk graph (UDG) is a graph $G=(V,E)$ obtained from a finite set $V\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ of points in the plane by joining two points $u,v$ by an edge if and only if their Euclidean distance satisfies $\|u-v\|\le 1$. A distributed algorithm on $G$ operates in synchronous rounds: each node $v\in V$ starts with a unique identifier and (possibly) its coordinates, and in each round every node may send a message to each neighbor and update its local state. After $k$ rounds, the output of $v$ may depend only on information gathered within its $k$-hop neighborhood; such an algorithm is called $k$-local, and the local complexity of a task is the smallest $k=k(n,\varepsilon,\dots)$ for which a correct (or $(1+\varepsilon)$-approximate) algorithm exists.

Determine the local complexity, as a function of the number of nodes $n$ and the desired approximation parameter $\varepsilon>0$, of fundamental coordination tasks on unit disk graphs under $k$-local communication. As a concrete benchmark, establish matching upper and lower bounds on the number of communication rounds required for a deterministic distributed algorithm to compute a $(1+\varepsilon)$-approximation to a minimum dominating set of a unit disk graph, both in the location-aware model (where each node knows its coordinates) and in the connectivity-only model (where nodes know only the graph structure and unique IDs).
artifact.category_tag: Distributed local algorithms on unit disk graphs
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made: local constant-factor approximation algorithms for dominating and connected dominating sets in UDGs are known, and local PTAS results exist for location-aware UDGs (Wattenhofer et al., Czyzowicz et al.). Lenzen, Pignolet, and Wattenhofer established asymptotically tight bounds on the time/approximation tradeoff for deterministic distributed algorithms on UDGs, showing in particular that $o(\log^* n)$ rounds do not suffice for a $(1+\varepsilon)$-approximate minimum dominating set. However, a complete characterization of the local complexity of all typical coordination tasks on UDGs remains open, so the broad question is only partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Local Algorithms for Dominating and Connected Dominating Sets of Unit Disk Graphs with Location Aware Nodes
status_evidence.snippet: Local, constant approximation deterministic algorithms for dominating (5-approx) and connected dominating (7.453+ε) sets in location-aware UDGs.
status_evidence.claim: Constant-factor local approximations exist for location-aware UDGs.

status_evidence.title: Local PTAS for Dominating and Connected Dominating Set in Location Aware Unit Disk Graph
status_evidence.snippet: Local 1+ε approximations for minimum dominating and connected dominating set in location aware UDGs.
status_evidence.claim: A local PTAS is known when nodes know their coordinates.

status_evidence.title: Distributed minimum dominating set approximations in restricted families of graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Asymptotically tight trade-off between time and approximation for deterministic distributed MDS on UDGs; o(log* n) rounds insufficient for (1+ε)-approximation.
status_evidence.claim: Tight time/approximation lower bounds are established for UDGs.
